reviews.review_title: Quirky MR Gem with Huge Potential! 🖐️
reviews.review_description:
Disembodied is... different, and it makes absolutely no attempt to hide it! Quirky, original, and full of personality, this game puts you in the role of two disembodied hands straight out of The Addams Family — think Thing T. Thing, but with both hands under your control!

The hand-tracking mechanics are what make this experience so special. You use your actual hands to move forward, turn, move backwards, climb, and collect items across multiple levels. Need to reach an object that's too high? Simply stretch your hands apart to extend your reach! Is a wall blocking your view? Move around in your physical space to guide your hands in the right direction and find a way through.

It's a clever concept that genuinely makes mixed reality and hand tracking feel meaningful rather than just being gimmicks. The gameplay encourages you to think spatially, experiment with your movements, and interact with the environment in unexpected ways.

Still in Early Access, Disembodied already shows huge potential. The concept is fresh, the mechanics work well, and there's plenty of room for this unusual little gem to grow into a real hit.

Well done to the developers for daring to do something different and making such creative use of mixed reality. I'm looking forward to seeing how this one evolves. Highly recommended for anyone looking for something genuinely original in VR!

A one-of-a-kind mixed reality game, it's got excellent hand-tracked gameplay, in fact the game is all about hands. The mechanics are as unique as they look on the trailers, you've got to experience it.

This game is certainly different, it is handtracking only which does take some getting used to a little fiddly at times but that is only as I have not mastered it yet.  You also need a well lit room for seamless hand tracking.  One to look at if you like unusual, and I am not sure there is another game like it.

This is a game like nothing else. Using your actual hands to navigate each level is like something out of a fever dream. The craziest part is that your real finger movements translate to the game. You can spider crawl with your fingers, go cowabunga style using only your thumb and pinky, or even flip the bird the entire time, moving with your middle finger only. The challenges can be tough, but they are fun and never feel impossible. The inclusion of the level editor really stretches out the game and lets you create cool levels.

The game is pretty unique and fun too even if I have only completed the tutorial so far, however I have noticed that the controls are buggy sometimes on my meta quest 2 and its best also as well to play in roomscale mode instead of stationary or seated and you need a well-lit room as well since this game relies heavily on hand-tracking. Overall, I would give it a higher rating if it had a slightly more stable physics engine and more responsive hand-tracking controls.
I love the mechanics in this game and it looks remarkable throughout, excellent job by the production team
